messages.subject: how to separate X chromosome
parts:
Dear All,

This may be very simple thing to do, but I don't know the way to do it.

The region that is no marker on the X chromosome is too long,
so I would like to separate it into two parts like autosome.

But I don't know the way to separate it while still recognizing X chr. 

Thank you for all your help!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: how to separate X chromosome
parts:
If you use movemarker() to move some of the X chromosome markers to a new chromosome, that new chromosome will also have class "X" and so treated as another X chromosome.
Here's an example:

data(hyper)
mapX <- pull.map(hyper, chr="X")[[1]]
for(i in 3:length(mapX)) {
    hyper <- movemarker(hyper, names(mapX)[i], "Xb", mapX[i])
}
summary(hyper)

It'll give a warning about having more than one X chromosome; I'm not totally sure that everything will work.

Alternatively, if you have a chromosome that's being treated like an autosome and you want it to be treated like an X chromosome, you can assign it class "X" like this:

    class(hyper$geno[["Xb"]]) <- "X"

karl
